categories.main_business_segments: Inui Global Logistics Co., Ltd. operates three main business segments: (1) International Shipping (Logistics), focusing on bulk cargo transport using owned and chartered vessels; (2) Warehousing and Transportation (Logistics), providing storage, document archiving, and cargo transportation services; and (3) Real Estate, primarily leasing residential and office properties in the Kachidoki area of Tokyo.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages efficient fleet management for its Handy-size bulk carriers, implements digital warehouse operation systems (SOS), and utilizes advanced logistics process improvements. In real estate, it applies disaster-resilient building methods and community-based property management. The company also emphasizes environmental compliance in shipping, such as fuel efficiency and emission regulations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include global commodity traders, manufacturers, and trading companies requiring bulk shipping (wood, cement, fertilizer, grain, slag, coke, etc.), as well as domestic businesses needing warehousing, document storage, and transportation. The real estate segment serves residential tenants and office lessees, mainly in central Tokyo.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally in shipping, with major routes covering Asia, Oceania, Europe, the Middle East, North and South America. Warehousing and transportation are concentrated in the Tokyo metropolitan area, while real estate assets are primarily located in the Kachidoki and Tsukishima districts of Tokyo. The company also has a significant presence in Panama through its shipping subsidiary.
categories.supply_chain_position: Inui Global Logistics operates both upstream and midstream in the supply chain: upstream as a vessel owner/operator in international shipping, and midstream as a provider of warehousing and transportation services. In real estate, it acts as a downstream asset holder and lessor.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening asset-driven business foundations, enhancing operational efficiency through digitalization and process improvement, and pursuing sustainability in logistics and shipping. The company is focused on adapting to environmental regulations, developing new logistics solutions for niche markets, and advancing urban redevelopment projects in its real estate segment. There is no significant traditional R&D activity reported.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through shipping freight charges and charter fees, warehousing and storage fees, transportation service charges, and rental income from real estate properties. The company also earns from asset sales and financial investments.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other Japanese and international bulk shipping companies, logistics providers, and real estate lessors in Tokyo. The company positions itself as a mid-sized, diversified logistics and real estate group with a unique combination of shipping, warehousing, and urban property assets, differentiating itself from pure-play operators.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated revenue was 31.77 billion yen, with operating profit of 3.66 billion yen and net profit attributable to shareholders of 5.02 billion yen. The company has shown revenue volatility due to shipping market cycles but achieved significant profit growth in FY2025, partly from asset sales. Total assets reached 74.9 billion yen, with a stable equity ratio near 50%.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Inui Global Logistics emphasizes its integrated logistics and real estate platform, combining stable asset-based income with flexible, customer-oriented logistics solutions. Its strengths include a resilient Handy-size shipping fleet, niche warehousing services resistant to automation, and prime Tokyo real estate assets. The company highlights its adaptability, sustainability initiatives, and community-focused property management as key differentiators.
